body:
<!-- plain-summary -->
A resilience test simulates an unreachable storage node by freezing its process, which is not the same as a real network outage where the node stays alive and keeps running on its own clock. This issue proposes adding a true network-partition fault to the test so Wyrd is exercised against the stronger, more realistic failure — important because a still-live but isolated node can attempt stale actions when the network heals, and future tests will involve more than dumb storage nodes.

**Summary.** The Tier-1 consistency-over-repair leg (ADR-0039, `crates/chunkstore-grpc/tests/tier1_jepsen_consistency.rs` + `xtask/src/faults.rs`) injects its "unreachable node" fault with `docker pause`/`unpause`. That is a **freezer-cgroup process freeze** (all processes in the container suspended), not a network-level partition — Jepsen treats `:pause` and `:partition` as distinct nemeses. Surfaced by review of PR #395 (the ADR-0039 ratification).

**Why it is adequate today.** Wyrd's D-servers are *dumb* storage (they initiate no commits of their own), so from the custodian repair path a paused D-server and a network-partitioned one are observably equivalent: the node is unreachable, repair proceeds around it, and the ADR-0015 contract must hold across the heal. ADR-0039 (as ratified) describes the mechanism honestly as a pause-based isolation fault and notes this upgrade as additive.

**Why upgrade anyway.** A network-level partition (drop packets via `iptables`/`tc`, or `docker network disconnect`) keeps the isolated node **live** — able to time out, expire leases on its own clock, and attempt a stale action on heal — a strictly stronger nemesis. It also matters more once any node on the isolated side is *not* dumb (e.g. a second custodian candidate, or the metadata/coordination tier in a future cross-tier drill). M7's failover/DR drills (proposal 0014) are the natural consumer.

**Scope.**
- [ ] add a packet-drop partition nemesis to `faults.rs` (keep pause as a separate, cheaper leg)
- [ ] assert the same ADR-0015 properties across a live-partition-and-heal
- [ ] wire it into the tier1-jepsen job (privileged, off the `xtask ci` merge gate per ADR-0016)

**Refs:** ADR-0039, #329 (the literal public Jepsen/Elle credibility artifact — separate), proposal 0014 (M7 drills), #250.

title: Upgrade the Tier-1 Jepsen isolation leg from docker pause to a network-level partition
